Posterior predictions from the target regression model

Source: R/predict.R
predict.bsm_fit.Rd

Computes, for each row of newdata, the posterior distribution of the target-model linear predictor (type = "link") or mean response (type = "response": \(x'\beta\), \(\mathrm{logit}^{-1}(x'\beta)\) or \(\exp(x'\beta)\)), using every retained posterior draw. This is the regression function of the population represented by the probability sample and the compatible NP units; it does not include observation-level noise.

Usage

# S3 method for class 'bsm_fit'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  type = c("response", "link"),
  interval = c("credible", "none"),
  level = 0.95,
  summary = TRUE,
  ...
)

# S3 method for class 'bsm_baseline'
predict(
  object,
  newdata,
  type = c("response", "link"),
  interval = c("credible", "none"),
  level = 0.95,
  summary = TRUE,
  ...
)

Arguments

object

A bsm_fit or bsm_baseline object.

newdata

Data frame (formula fits) or design matrix (matrix fits) at which to predict. Required.

type

"response" (default) or "link".

interval

"credible" (default) to add equal-tailed credible limits, or "none".

level

Credible-interval level.

summary

If FALSE, return the full matrix of posterior draws (draws in rows, observations in columns) instead of summaries.

...

Not used.

Value

A data frame with columns fit (posterior mean) and, if requested, lwr and upr; or a matrix of draws when summary = FALSE.

Examples

d <- simulate_mixture_data("binomial", n_prob = 150, n_nonprob = 150,
                           contamination = 0.3, seed = 7)
fit <- mixture_fit(y ~ x1, d$prob, d$nonprob, family = "binomial",
                   n_iter = 500, burnin = 200, seed = 1)
predict(fit, newdata = data.frame(x1 = c(-1, 0, 1)))
#>         fit       lwr       upr
#> 1 0.3760308 0.2326381 0.5099556
#> 2 0.5514263 0.4528796 0.6349134
#> 3 0.7154087 0.6233067 0.8109616
